newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrials end at new high on Dow, Stals.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrials end at new high on Dow, Stals.

text.p: South African industrial shares finished stronger on Thursday, propelled higher by positive sentiment from Wall Street and other world market's recent rallies, dealers said.

They said Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments this week that interest rates could be cut before the end of the year also continued to fuel local and offshore buying interest on the industrials.

Reiterating his Wednesday's remarks, Stals told Reuters on Thursday he believed that recent inflation and money supply data was encouraging and could pave the way for a rate cut before the end of the year.
But he added that it was impossible to be precise about when conditions would be right to cut the key Bank rate from its current 17 percent level.

The industrial index finished up 28.1 points at 9,150.5 -- a new life high, with golds taking no cue from industrials' jovial mood as bullion continued to struggle to break through the $328 an ounce resistance level.
The gold index dropped 1.2 points to 981.4, while the all-shares climbed 10.8 points to 7,484.5.

Dealers said Thursday's currency weakness, which saw the rand weaken to a six month low of 4.61, had been largely ignored as the currency had already been discounted to soften to around 4.65 by the end of the year.
Overall market volumes were high with 80.3 million shares worth around 985 million rand changing hands in a market expected to remain buoyant on Friday.
